title: Lord, We Thy Will Obey
description: Lord, We Thy Will Obey in Tonic Solfa to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 533.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), and this page sets them to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR); any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, we thy will o-bey, And in thy plea-sure rest; We, on-ly we, can say, "What-ev-er is, is best;" Joy-ful to meet, will-ing to part, Con-vinced we still are one in heart.

lines: Joyful to meet, willing to part,
Convinced we still are one in heart.
And cry, in answer to thy call,
"Thou art, O Christ, our all in all!"
We cannot want, if thou art here.
And live and die wrapped up in thee!

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
